newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu wants Israeli probe of corruption report.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu wants Israeli probe of corruption report.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Friday for a police inquiry into allegations by state-owned television of corruption in his government's short-lived appointment of an attorney general.

"Things like this cannot be left hanging in the air," Netanyahu's office quoted him as telling a cabinet meeting. "Therefore I propose a quick and thorough police investigation to reach the truth of the matter as quickly as possible."

The television said on Wednesday that Netanyahu had appointed lawyer Roni Bar-On as attorney general two weeks ago at the behest of Arye Deri, an ex-cabinet minister on trial for corruption charges, whose Shas party is a key coalition member.
The television said Bar-On promised Deri a plea bargain in his trial in return for Shas giving Netanyahu vital support for a deal with the PLO on redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Bar-On resigned within 12 hours of taking office under public criticism he was unfit for the job. Bar-On denied the television's allegations, as did Netanyahu and Deri.
"I was astonished when I heard these (allegations)," Netanyahu was quoted as telling the cabinet. "To the best of my knowledge they have no foundation."
